text: Input identity check: actual Q is Zhao et al., Learning-Augmented Algorithms survey (inputs/Q.tex:51,106-113); actual P is the anonymous From Truthful Peer Signals to Contribution Rankings interface paper (inputs/P.tex:12-31). P internally calls other papers Q and P, so its internal labels must not be mistaken for this assigned pair. I will test whether the survey’s system-level composition and prediction-cost framework yields a concrete theorem or failure mode for the interface paper.

Initial read: the supplied inputs are Q = Zhao et al., a survey of learning-augmented algorithms, and P = an essay titled 'From Truthful Peer Signals to Contribution Rankings'. P's internal labels 'Q' and 'P' instead denote two other papers (mechanism design and MARS-RA), so its stated Q/P interface is not an interface with the supplied Q. I will treat the supplied files as the actual pair, audit P's claims against Q's prediction/robustness/composition framework, and look for a precise new question without accepting P's embedded pair labels.

Possible new line for the assigned pair: turn P’s population calibration into Q’s error-dependent prediction interface. Define a declared contamination/error metric for shared-draw peer moments and edge means, propagate it through triangle/path reliability calibration, Bradley--Terry logit, and the comparison-graph Laplacian to a score error; then price repeated co-label queries as Q urges (Q:963-980,1095-1109,1242-1258; P:78-110,134-156). A crucial negative boundary: passing P’s moment checks need not certify the latent target when peers share common-mode bias. I am working out the exact bound and counterexample before choosing the main claim.

Independent objection/identifiability counterexample (supplied Q = LAA survey, supplied P = conditional interface note). P lines 68-110 requires reports conditionally independent given the same realised latent comparison and concludes connected comparison graph identifies scores; P lines 139-144 acknowledges correlated errors break factorisation. Moment diagnostics alone cannot test that premise. On a four-vertex path, set edge score differences in orientation \(1\!\to\!2\!\to\!3\!\to\!4\) to \((4,-1.5,-1.5)\), so true \(c_1-c_4=1>0\). In world A, each item has a common hidden flip \(B\) with \(\mathbb E B=b=1/2\), and reports \(Y_r=X B Z_r\) with independent positive-reliability \(Z_r\). Then all peer agreement moments still equal \(a_ra_s\), while report means equal \(a_rb\tanh((c_i-c_j)/2)\). World B takes \(X'=XB\) as the latent BT comparison, with path edge differences \(f_b(d)=2\operatorname{artanh}(b\tanh(d/2))\), and independent peer flips \(Z_r\). The entire observable report law is identical in both worlds; world B satisfies P's assumptions. Yet \(c'_1-c'_4=f_{1/2}(4)-2f_{1/2}(1.5)\approx-0.26458<0\), reversing the true order. Thus on a merely connected comparison graph, neither unlimited repeated reports nor rank-one agreement checks certify the latent ranking against common-mode error. This sharpens Q's warning that prediction error may be partly unobservable (Q 970-980) and cannot be transferred downstream without an explicit error premise (Q 1097-1110).

Proposed distinct direction for this assigned pair: characterize when P's crowdsourced ordinal predictor can be audited before it enters Q's learning-augmented decision layer. The four-node path counterexample in entry 4 shows that P's connectedness plus rank-one moment fit is not an observable certificate of ranking accuracy under common-mode noise. A targeted extra comparison of vertices \(1\) and \(4\) would expose that example: its direct report mean has positive sign, while the path-inferred BT difference has negative sign. Candidate publishable question: for a budgeted comparison graph and a specified correlated-error class, what minimal audit edges or trusted anchors make ranking error observable enough to obtain Q-style downstream smoothness/robustness? I am checking the scope: full pairwise coverage preserves ordinal signs under a positive common symmetric flip, though score magnitudes remain confounded; this needs a precise model rather than a blanket impossibility claim. Q 345-401 types rankings as ordinal predictions and warns the error metric matters; Q 963-980 and 1242-1258 require accounting for feedback/query cost; P 64-110 supplies the two-graph calibration construction.

I derived a conditional finite-sample bridge, in emmy/working_note.md. For clean reliabilities (a_r\geq\alpha>0), edge probabilities (p_e\in[\tau,1-\tau]), overlap-tree depth (D), moment error (\delta), and comparison Laplacian (L_G), set (u=2\delta/\alpha^2), (T=(D+3/2)u), (h=\delta e^T/\alpha+e^T-1). If (\delta\leq\alpha^2/2) and (h\leq\tau), P’s triangle/path estimator followed by logit and least-squares inversion obeys (\|\widehat c-c\|_2\leq\sqrt{|E|/\lambda_2(L_G)}\,h/[\tau(1-\tau/2)]). This follows by log-moment Lipschitzness, path propagation, mean division, logit derivative, and incidence pseudoinverse. With (N) independent repeats per measured population and (M) moments, (\delta\leq b+\sqrt{2\log(2M/\zeta)/N}) simultaneously with probability (1-\zeta), where (b) is model-misspecification bias; a direct plan costs at most (N(2|L_H|+|E|)) labels. Sources: P:64-110,132-156; Q:260-265,1095-1109,1242-1258. This is an upper bound with explicit assumptions, not a policy or truthfulness theorem.

Math rendering correction to entry 6: \(u=2\delta/\alpha^2\), \(T=(D+3/2)u\), \(h=\delta e^T/\alpha+e^T-1\), and \(\|\widehat c-c\|_2\leq\sqrt{|E|/\lambda_2(L_G)}\,h/[\tau(1-\tau/2)]\). The concentration radius is \(b+\sqrt{2\log(2M/\zeta)/N}\). The file emmy/working_note.md contains the full derivation with TeX delimiters.

Cross-check of ada entries 4-5: the common flip construction is sound. On a tree, each transformed edge mean \(b\tanh(d_e/2)\) gives a valid alternative Bradley--Terry edge difference \(f_b(d_e)=2\operatorname{artanh}(b\tanh(d_e/2))\); independence fails conditional on intended \(X_e\) but holds conditional on \(X_eB\), and all observed joint report laws coincide. Numerically \(f_{1/2}(4)-2f_{1/2}(1.5)\approx-0.265\), while the true path sum is \(1\). The extra \(1\)-\(4\) edge detects this particular common-flip model because it imposes an inconsistent cycle, but neither cycle checks nor unlimited labels certify the intended target against unrestricted shared bias. My stability bound has an unobservable bias term \(b\) relative to the intended target; on the path this term does not shrink with \(N\). This favors a joint line: graph-aware cost/error bounds conditional on a declared bias class, plus audit or anchor design that makes that bias identifiable.

Detailed derivation of the observationally identical common-flip worlds is in ada/common_mode_counterexample.md. It proves a minimax ordinal error probability of at least \(1/2\) for the four-vertex path, regardless of sample count, when correlated common-mode flips are allowed. The observer-overlap triangle does not help because peer products cancel the common flip. An added direct comparison of vertices \(1\) and \(4\) exposes this specific instance via a Bradley--Terry cycle inconsistency. Scope: this does not refute P's theorem, whose conditional-independence assumption world A violates; it refutes any claim that P's observable rank-one agreement checks alone validate that assumption or certify ranking quality.

New positive extension after cross-checking ada entry 9: under the restricted misspecification \(Y_{er}=X_eB_eZ_{er}\), with a shared item-level sign \(B_e\) independent of \(X_e\), constant mean \(b=\mathbb E B_e>0\), and peer flips \(Z_{er}\) of constant positive reliability, P still calibrates \(a_r\) from peer agreements. Calibrated edge means are \(w_{ij}=b\tanh((c_i-c_j)/2)\). A nondegenerate comparison triangle \(i,j,k\) identifies \(b^2\) without target labels: \[b^2=\frac{w_{ik}w_{ij}w_{jk}}{w_{ij}+w_{jk}-w_{ik}},\] by the hyperbolic-tangent addition identity. Positive \(b\) fixes the root; every edge difference is then \(2\operatorname{artanh}(w_{ij}/b)\), and connectedness recovers \(c\) up to translation. This turns ada’s audit edge from a mere inconsistency check into a self-calibration device in a precisely declared correlated-error class. Degenerate triangles, edge-dependent \(b_e\), and unrestricted common bias remain unresolved. I will verify assumptions and add a derivation.

Strengthening entry 4: under the restricted misspecification \(Y_{er}=X_eB_eZ_{er}\) with edge-independent \(0<b=\mathbb E B_e<1\), the score transform on any tree is \(d'_e=f_b(d_e)=2\operatorname{artanh}(b\tanh(d_e/2))\). Universal preservation of every pairwise score order holds for a tree of diameter at most \(2\): any pair's path has at most two edges, and since \(f_b\) is odd and strictly increasing, \(\operatorname{sgn}(f_b(x)+f_b(y))=\operatorname{sgn}(x+y)\). Conversely any tree of diameter at least \(3\) contains a 3-edge path. Put differences \((2t+1,-t,-t)\) there and zero on other edges. The true endpoint difference is \(1>0\), but as \(t\to\infty\), the inferred difference tends to \(-2\operatorname{artanh}(b)<0\), so for large \(t\) order reverses. Thus star trees are exactly the connected comparison trees whose ordinal ranking is universally invariant under this positive shared-flip model; any longer tree can fail while passing every peer-agreement check. This is a precise graph-design statement, separate from emmy's clean-model finite-sample stability bound.

Prior-work check (queries: 'Bradley Terry ranking tree comparison graph common label noise rank identifiability correlated annotators'; 'pairwise comparison graph tree monotone link transformation ranking preservation star graph'; 'crowdsourcing correlated workers shared bias Dawid Skene identifiability pairwise ranking graph'; 'arxiv correlated annotators shared errors identifiability crowdsourcing label aggregation'; 'site:proceedings.mlr.press crowdsourcing correlated annotators identifiability'; 'Bradley Terry common flip noise comparison graph identifiability ranking'). Existing primary work treats correlated annotators (Li, Rubinstein & Cohn, ICML 2019, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/li19i.html), pairwise-co-occurrence identification under a Dawid--Skene model (Ibrahim et al., NeurIPS 2019, https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2019/hash/c0e19ce0dbabbc0d17a4f8d4324cc8e3-Abstract.html), and semi-verified learning with a few true values (Meister & Valiant, COLT 2018, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v75/meister18a.html). These confirm that correlation modeling and anchors are established themes. I did not locate this exact tree-diameter/common-flip ordinal statement in those queries, but that is not a novelty claim. Publication scope should be graph-aware audit/query design plus a downstream decision theorem, with full related-work review.

Verified the positive extension in emmy/working_note.md. Under \(Y_{er}=X_eB_eZ_{er}\), independent \(B_e\) with common mean \(b\in(0,1]\), and independent peer flips of mean \(a_r>0\), agreements remain \(q_{rs}=a_ra_s\). After P calibration, \(w_{ij}=\mathbb E Y_{er}/a_r=b\tanh((c_i-c_j)/2)\). For a comparison triangle set \(A=w_{ij}\), \(B=w_{jk}\), \(C=w_{ik}\). Then \(C=(A+B)/(1+AB/b^2)\), so \(b^2=ABC/(A+B-C)\) if \(ABC\ne0\). A positive root and connected graph recover all score differences. On a tree, every admissible \(b>\max_e|w_e|\) gives alternative integrable edge differences \(2\operatorname{artanh}(w_e/b)\); ada entry 4 supplies a ranking reversal. This is a precise candidate advance: one nondegenerate audit triangle identifies a uniform shared flip that defeats P on a tree. It does not handle edge-dependent bias, degenerate triangles, incentives, or downstream policy performance. Preliminary prior-work queries: Bradley Terry common flip noise triangle cycle identify noise rate pairwise comparisons; Bradley-Terry symmetric noise cycle identification. [Crowd-BT](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~xchen3/images/crowd_pairwise.pdf) already models worker-dependent symmetric mistakes and joint Bradley--Terry fitting, so novelty of this special case remains unverified.

Cross-check of emmy entry 10: the triangle formula is algebraically correct when \(w_{ij}w_{jk}w_{ik}\neq0\) and \(w_{ij}+w_{jk}-w_{ik}\neq0\). Writing \(u=w_{ij}\), \(v=w_{jk}\), \(w=w_{ik}\), the BT addition law under constant common attenuation gives \(w=(u+v)/(1+uv/b^2)\), hence \(b^2=wuv/(u+v-w)\). A triangle with three distinct score levels and nonzero endpoint difference meets this nondegeneracy. This is a useful repair within the *specified* shared-flip model, not a test of whether that model is true. For the four-node path example, adding chord \((1,3)\) or \((2,4)\) creates a calibrating triangle; adding \((1,4)\) only creates a four-cycle and exposes the particular inconsistency. The tree-diameter result remains a no-extra-query ordinal guarantee when only common positive attenuation is assumed.

Important interface distinction: Q explicitly lists ordinal rankings as prediction objects (Q 345-384), while supplied P recovers numerical Bradley--Terry scores to form a shaping potential (P 47-61, 100-110). My tree-diameter theorem protects only pairwise order under common positive attenuation, not score differences or P's shaping magnitudes. A Q-style downstream algorithm whose theorem depends solely on an inversion-count error could use the star-tree result; P's potential-shaping stage would need separate sensitivity to score distortion. This sharpens the publication question from 'are scores identifiable?' to 'what is the cheapest comparison design that identifies exactly the prediction object a specified downstream theorem consumes?'

Cross-check of ada entry 11: for any odd strictly increasing \(f\), \(\operatorname{sgn}(f(x)+f(y))=\operatorname{sgn}(x+y)\), since \(f(x)+f(y)=f(x)-f(-y)\). Thus positive uniform common flips preserve all pair orders on a star (paths of at most two edges), although \(b\) and score magnitudes remain unidentified. Three-edge paths permit reversals as ada shows. This sharpens the design target: audit triangles are needed for cardinal score calibration under the restricted model, while ordinal correctness can already hold on star trees; a claim that every tree loses ranking would be false.

Synthesis for assigned Q/P (question sharpened): What is the least costly comparison design that makes the *specific prediction object consumed downstream* identifiable under a declared shared-error class, with an error bound that can enter Q’s performance contract? P supplies two graphs and clean population inversion (P:64-110); Q requires a specified error metric, sensitivity, and prediction cost (Q:260-265, 973-980, 1095-1109, 1242-1258). Under constant positive common flips, star comparison trees preserve order but not magnitudes (ada 11,15); longer trees can reverse order while all peer moments fit (ada 4,9); one nondegenerate comparison triangle identifies the common flip and cardinal BT scores (emmy 13, ada 14). My note gives a clean-model finite-sample score bound and an unobservable bias floor. The candidate publication is a graph/query-cost frontier for ordinal versus cardinal targets under this restricted noise model, with a downstream decision theorem. Unresolved: novelty beyond prior noisy-ranking work, finite-sample stability of triangle calibration, minimal design beyond the sufficient triangle, strategic truthfulness, model validation against unrestricted bias, and sensitivity of P’s shaping policy. No claim of a complete end-to-end guarantee.
ready at #17

Correction to P's limitation wording: P line 141 says 'Correlated errors ... destroy the factorisation used here.' As a universal statement about the *observable* agreement identity this is false: in the common-item flip model from ada entry 4, reports are correlated conditional on intended \(X_e\), yet \(\mathbb E[Y_{er}Y_{es}]=a_ra_s\) exactly. The failure is subtler: the factorization can survive while \(\mathbb E[Y_{er}]/a_r=b\tanh((c_i-c_j)/2)\) targets an attenuated latent comparison. P's theorem remains correct under its stated conditional-independence assumption; its limitation sentence should say correlation can invalidate the identification, including without a visible agreement failure. This is the direct claim in P that the pair's error-observability lens from Q (Q 970-980, 1097-1110) sharpens.

Ada's final assessment of the supplied Q/P pair: the strongest supported line is a *prediction-object-aware comparison design* problem. Q's survey requires a declared ordinal or cardinal error, a downstream sensitivity argument, and prediction-query cost (Q 345-401, 963-980, 1097-1110, 1242-1258). Supplied P gives population score inversion from calibrated peer labels (P 64-110) but no finite-sample or downstream theorem (P 132-156). Under a constant positive item-level common flip, P's peer agreement moments still factorize (correction #19); on a comparison tree, ordinal order is universally preserved exactly for diameter at most \(2\), while longer trees can reverse it (#11). A nondegenerate comparison triangle identifies the common flip and restores cardinal scores under that restricted class (#13-14). The proof and explicit four-node indistinguishability example are in ada/common_mode_counterexample.md; style and math-delimiter checks pass. This is a credible publication direction, not a complete publishable result: minimal designs for general graphs, finite-sample stability/cost frontier, end-to-end policy sensitivity, strategic truthfulness, validation against unrestricted shared bias, and thorough prior-work comparison remain unresolved. I agree with emmy's #17 synthesis on this scope.
ready at #20

Correction/refinement to #14 and #17: a nondegenerate four-cycle also self-calibrates the uniform shared flip; a triangle is sufficient but not necessary. Orient four cycle edges consistently and write calibrated means \(w_1,\ldots,w_4\). BT cycle consistency requires \(\sum_i 2\operatorname{artanh}(w_i/b)=0\), equivalently \(S_1 b^2+S_3=0\), where \(S_1=\sum_iw_i\) and \(S_3=\sum_{i<j<k}w_iw_jw_k\). If \(S_1\ne0\), then \(b^2=-S_3/S_1\); the positive admissible root is unique. For ada’s path example, adding direct \((1,4)\) gives \(w\approx(0.4820,-0.3176,-0.3176,-0.2311)\), \(S_1\approx-0.3842\), \(S_3\approx0.09605\), and \(b^2=0.25\). When \(S_1=S_3=0\), the cycle equation holds for every admissible \(b\), so it does not identify the rate. This matters for the minimal audit-design question: any informative short cycle may suffice, not only a triangle. Assumptions remain constant positive \(b\), BT edge law, and calibrated means; unrestricted shared bias is not certified.

Emmy entry #22 reopens the minimal audit-design question: I will verify the four-cycle identity, test whether one longer cycle identifies the uniform common-flip rate, and update the supported graph-design claim. The relevant model remains \(Y_{er}=X_eB_eZ_{er}\) with edge-independent \(b=\mathbb E B_e>0\), not unrestricted correlated bias.

I added the four-cycle proof and numerical check to emmy/working_note.md; style-ban-artifacts and style-gate both pass. This extends the #17 design line without changing its scope: P:64-110 supplies calibrated peer means and BT inversion; P:139-144 understates the possibility that correlated common noise leaves agreement factorization intact; Q:345-401 distinguishes ordinal from cardinal predictions, and Q:1095-1109,1242-1258 demand an error-transfer premise and a query cost. A four-cycle with \(S_1\ne0\) identifies the uniform shared attenuation \(b\) exactly at population level; a tree never identifies its magnitude, though star trees preserve ranking. Remaining gaps are finite-sample cycle conditioning, graph/query minimax design, a downstream theorem, strategic elicitation, and model validation beyond constant \(b\). The publication question is now best phrased as a prediction-object-aware audit frontier rather than triangle-only calibration.
ready at #24

Cross-check and extension of emmy #22-24: the four-cycle identity is correct. For a consistently oriented comparison cycle with calibrated means \(w_e=b\tanh(d_e/2)\), BT consistency is \(\sum_e 2\operatorname{artanh}(w_e/b)=0\). Writing \(S_k\) for elementary symmetric sums, a four-cycle gives \(S_1b^2+S_3=0\), so \(S_1\neq0\) identifies its positive admissible rate. But a five- or six-cycle gives \(S_1b^4+S_3b^2+S_5=0\) and can have two admissible rates. Explicit six-cycle: \(w=(-65,60,-52,-23,62,16)/100\), \(S_1=-1/50\), \(S_3=12749/500000\), \(S_5=-497471/62500000\). Its two rates are \(b\approx0.738909\) and \(b\approx0.853765\), both greater than \(\max|w_e|=0.65\). Integrating \(d_e(b)=2\operatorname{artanh}(w_e/b)\) gives \(c_3-c_6\approx+0.042834\) under the first and \(-0.126036\) under the second. Both constant-common-flip worlds induce the same entire observable report law, so even one redundant cycle need not identify the ranking. Derivation and exact data are in ada/common_mode_counterexample.md; style checks pass. This narrows the audit frontier: a nondegenerate triangle or four-cycle suffices for cardinal calibration, whereas a longer single cycle can leave ordinal ambiguity.

General ordinal sufficiency under the same uniform positive common-flip model: any connected comparison graph of diameter at most \(2\) identifies every pairwise score order from calibrated edge means even if \(b\) is not identified. For each vertex pair, choose a path of at most two edges; \(d_e(b)=2\operatorname{artanh}(w_e/b)\) is odd and strictly increasing in \(w_e\), so \(\operatorname{sgn}(d_1(b)+d_2(b))=\operatorname{sgn}(w_1+w_2)\) for every admissible \(b>0\). Thus a five-cycle can have two cardinal calibrations but retains one ranking, whereas the six-cycle in #26 has diameter \(3\) and reverses a pair. This extends the prior star-tree statement, not a converse for arbitrary graphs: triangles and four-cycles can identify \(b\) even in large-diameter graphs. The distinction matters because Q 345-384 treats ordinal and point predictions separately; P 100-110 supplies cardinal BT scores for shaping.
